memoryText: And there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Acts 4:12 slowly, several times, and say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Peter says this to the Jewish council that condemned Jesus. Hours earlier, he had been arrested, and now he stands before the same rulers, filled with the Holy Spirit.

“And there is salvation in no one else.” This is a bold and exclusive claim. Peter does not say Jesus is one of many ways. He says salvation is found in him alone. This was not popular in the first century, and it is not popular now. But it is the heart of the gospel.

“For there is no other name under heaven.” The name stands for the person, his authority and character. There is no other person anywhere who can do what Jesus does.

“Given among men.” Salvation is a gift. God gave this name. We did not discover it by our efforts.

“By which we must be saved.” The word “must” shows the necessity. We need saving. We cannot save ourselves. And there is a name by which we can be saved.

This verse is a comfort and a commission. It comforts because the way to God is open in Jesus. It commissions because if there is no other name, then people need to hear it.

When you are tempted to doubt that Jesus is enough, or when you are unsure about speaking of him, say this verse.
weekInReview: This week you read Peter’s healing at the Beautiful Gate, his bold preaching, and his words to the council: “There is salvation in no other name.” You saw the early church share its possessions, and you saw the hypocrisy of Ananias and Sapphira. You watched seven men be chosen to serve. Three psalms about the exalted Christ framed Peter’s sermons: Psalm 2, in which the LORD sets his King on Zion and the nations rage in vain; Psalm 16, in which God does not abandon his holy one to Sheol; and Psalm 110, in which the Lord sits at God’s right hand as priest and king. Finally, you saw Stephen preach to the council, see Jesus standing in heaven, and forgive his murderers as he died. A young man named Saul stood by. A great persecution scattered the church.
reflectionQuestions: Peter and John said, “We cannot but speak of what we have seen and heard.” What have you seen and heard of Jesus that you cannot keep to yourself?
Stephen forgave those who killed him, as Jesus did. Who is one person you need to forgive, and what would it take to pray for them?
The psalms of the week show Christ reigning at God’s right hand. How does knowing that he is on the throne give you courage in the thing you fear most?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus that there is salvation in no other name, and that you have found it.
Ask him for the boldness of Peter.
